false_positives.pattern: False positives cluster around legitimate role-framing prompts ('act as', 'you are') and instruction-heavy NLP tasks. These share surface vocabulary with injections (role_swap_keyword_count, override_keyword_count) but lack the filter-bypass or data-exfil signals that distinguish genuine attacks. The model cannot yet distinguish persona framing in creative/educational context from hostile role-hijacking.

false_negatives.pattern: False negatives cluster in three categories: (1) multilingual injections (German, French) where all override keywords appear in a foreign language and score zero on the English keyword features; (2) low-keyword indirect attacks using narrative or hypothetical framing ('let's play a game', 'imagine you are') that avoid the keyword vocabulary entirely; (3) short imperative injections ('forget everything', 'repeat after me') that are too terse to accumulate structural signal. All three share near-zero scores on f01–f04 keyword features, so the model's primary signal is absent.

adversarial.summary: The adversarial set contains 17 injections and 8 benign FP-trap examples. The model catches 64.7% of injections (recall on adversarial set) vs 56.0% overall accuracy. Multilingual and narrative-framed examples are the hardest cases.
